title: The Slow Motion Developer: When Agentic Coding Makes Your Fingers Feel Like Stone
body_markdown:
You return to vanilla VS Code after a week of agentic coding, and the world has slowed down. Not your mind — your fingers. The cognitive gap between architecture-level thinking and line-by-line typing creates a dissonance that feels like wearing gloves while playing piano.

The role shift is irreversible once experienced. Developers who go through the agentic transformation stop being typists and become architects. Focus moves to data flow, feature structuring, component communication; syntax and repetitive logic are delegated to AI. The basic Copilot suggestions pale in comparison to full-agent orchestration — it's the difference between a paintbrush and a mural.

Cursor 3.0 runs multiple simultaneous AI assistants. Claude Code operates as an independent engineer with terminal and desktop access. OpenAI Codex serves as the big-picture manager. Google Antigravity v2.0 enters the arena. Microsoft is integrating agents directly into VS Code's preview window — the IDE itself becomes the orchestration layer.

But there are costs to this transformation. Junior developers lose hands-on typing experience, which means less muscle memory for debugging later. The "vibe coding" approach creates architectural debt that human review must eventually surface. Raw control matters: for deep debugging and legacy projects, explicit knowledge of every line prevents catastrophic misunderstandings.

Claude Code's maintenance script philosophy offers a counterweight: build transparent, verifiable routines where scripts are designed for human inspection first, execution second. Dry-run patterns become critical safety habits. Precise prompting dramatically improves reliability — vague requests fail, structured requests with exact paths and exclusion rules succeed.

The goblin watches developers caught between two eras: the old world of keystroke mastery and the new world of architectural oversight. Neither is superior; they are simply different phases of the same evolution. The slow motion feeling isn't weakness — it's the friction of cognitive upgrade.
